reason: While the text does indicate the Israelites are suffering (צַעֲקַת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּאָה אֵלַי - 'the cry of the children of Israel has come to me' and הַלַּחַץ אֲשֶׁר מִצְרַיִם לֹחֲצִים אֹתָם - 'the oppression with which the Egyptians are oppressing them'), the text explicitly attributes their suffering to Egyptian oppression, not to their own fault. God recognizes their affliction as something the Egyptians are inflicting upon them, and responds with compassion by calling Moses to deliver them. There is no suggestion in this passage that the Israelites are responsible for their own suffering.
